description: The line plot titled "BBQ" compares the accuracy of different models as a function of the number of demonstrations on the 'BBQ' task. The x-axis, labeled '#Demonstrations', has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1500 with tick labels at intervals of 250 demonstrations. The y-axis, labeled 'Accuracy', has a linear scale ranging from 45 to 55 with tick labels at intervals of 5. The 'Squared Exponential' model starts at an accuracy of approximately 52 at 0 demonstrations, increases steadily to 56 at 250 demonstrations, and then stabilizes. The 'Tanh' model begins at about 48 accuracy at 0 demonstrations and shows a slight decline to 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'ELU' model starts at 46 accuracy and shows a gradual increase to 48 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'LLmA-2-chat-7B' model maintains a consistent accuracy of 43 across all demonstration points, performing significantly worse than the other models. The 'Squared Exponential' model consistently outperforms all other models, with the 'ELU' model showing the second-best performance overall.
